section.header: Grade of Vice Chief of the National Guard Bureau
section.text: Section 10505 of title 10, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection:

paragraph.text: The Vice Chief of the National Guard Bureau shall be appointed to serve in the grade of general.

The Secretary of Defense shall designate, pursuant to subsection (b) of section 526 of this title, the position of Vice Chief of the National Guard Bureau as one of the general officer and flag officer positions to be excluded from the limitations in subsection (a) of such section.

section.header: Transfers of officers between the active and inactive National Guard
section.text: Section 303 of title 32, United States Code, is amended by inserting after subsection (c) the following new subsections:

subsection.text: Under regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Army—

paragraph.text: an officer of the Army National Guard who fills a vacancy in a federally recognized unit of the Army National Guard may be transferred from the active Army National Guard to the inactive Army National Guard;

an officer of the Army National Guard transferred to the inactive Army National Guard pursuant to paragraph (1) may be transferred from the inactive Army National Guard to the active Army National Guard to fill a vacancy in a federally recognized unit;

a warrant officer of the Army National Guard who fills a vacancy in a federally recognized unit of the Army National Guard may be transferred from the active Army National Guard to the inactive Army National Guard; and

a warrant officer of the Army National Guard transferred to the inactive Army National Guard pursuant to paragraph (1) may be transferred from the inactive Army National Guard to the active Army National Guard to fill a vacancy in a federally recognized unit.

subsection.text: Under regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Air Force—

paragraph.text: an officer of the Air National Guard who fills a vacancy in a federally recognized unit of the Air National Guard may be transferred from the active Air National Guard to the inactive Air National Guard; and

an officer of the Air National Guard transferred to the inactive Air National Guard pursuant to paragraph (1) may be transferred from the inactive Air National Guard to the active Air National Guard to fill a vacancy in a federally recognized unit.

section.header: Authorization for FireGuard Program

subsection.text: Chapter 5 of title 32, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new section:

section.header: Authorization for FireGuard Program

subsection.text: The Secretary of Defense may use members of the National Guard to carry out a program to aggregate, analyze, and assess multi-source remote sensing information for interagency partnerships in the detection and monitoring of wildfires, and to support any emergency response to such wildfires. Such a program shall be known as the FireGuard Program.
If the Secretary carries out a program under this section, the Secretary—

paragraph.text: shall transfer the functions, personnel, assets, and capabilities of the FireGuard Program, in existence on the day before the date of enactment of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024, to the FireGuard Program authorized under this section;
may direct the Director of the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency to provide such assistance as the Secretary determines necessary to carry out the FireGuard Program; and
may not reduce support, or transfer responsibility for support to an interagency partner, for the FireGuard Program authorized under this section.

subsection.text: The table of sections at the beginning of such chapter is amended by adding at the end the following new item:

toc.toc-entry: 510. Authorization for FireGuard Program.

subsection.text: The National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (Public Law 117–81) is amended by striking section 515.

section.header: Designation of at least one general officer of the Marine Corps Reserve as a joint qualified officer
section.text: The Secretary of Defense shall ensure that at least one general officer of the Marine Corps Reserve is designated as a joint qualified officer.

section.header: Report on foreign disclosure officer and foreign military sales officer billets

subsection.text: Congress—

paragraph.text: recognizes the critical importance of the Australia-United Kingdom-United States (hereinafter referred to as AUKUS) trilateral agreement;
believes that appropriate staffing in the Department of Defense must be committed to ensuring its success;
finds that more seamless and expedient transfer of advanced defense technologies both to and from allies and partners is—

subparagraph.text: in the national security interest of the United States; and
critical to ensuring retention of a technological edge over adversaries;

paragraph.text: exhorts the Secretary of Defense to commit resources to ensuring full-time equivalents and billets for foreign disclosure officers as well as foreign military sales officers in the Department are fully staffed to support the fulsome review and expedient transfer of defense articles to AUKUS parties; and
encourages the Secretary of Defense to prioritize the hiring and retention of individuals in these roles.

subsection.text: Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the congressional defense committees a report identifying gaps in the level of staffing necessary to accomplish AUKUS-related efforts in the Department of Defense, including those described in subsection (a). The report shall also include—

paragraph.text: an assessment of any personnel shortfalls;
a detailed plan for ensuring that existing positions described in subsection (a) are prioritized for hiring and retention;
an assessment of future staffing needs to ensure the noted goal of more rapid technology transfer to AUKUS parties;

a plan for the implementation of the recommendations included in the report, including an explanation of any additional funding, authorities, or organizational changes needed for the implementation of such recommendations; and
any other matters determined appropriate by the Secretary.

subtitle.header: General Service Authorities and Military Records

section.header: Requirement to classify certain persons as unaccounted for from World War II under certain conditions
section.text: Section 1509 of title 10, United States Code, is amended—

paragraph.text: by redesignating subsection (f) as subsection (g); and
by inserting after subsection (e), the following new subsection:

With respect to a person described in subsection (a)(1) whom the designated Agency Director determined is accounted for, such designated Agency Director shall determine such person to be unaccounted for if the identification, by a practitioner of an appropriate forensic science, of remains as those of such person, demonstrated discrepancies.
Upon request of the primary next of kin of a person whom the designated Agency Director determined unaccounted for pursuant to paragraph (1), the designated Agency Director shall—

subparagraph.text: exhume the remains of such person; and
direct the senior medical examiner assigned or detailed under subsection (b)(2) to investigate such remains using state-of-the-art technology.

section.header: Authority to designate certain separated members of the Air Force as honorary separated members of the Space Force
section.text: Chapter 933 of title 10, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new section:

section.header: Authority to designate certain separated members of the Air Force as honorary separated members of the Space Force

subsection.text: The Secretary of the Air Force may prescribe regulations that authorize an eligible individual to be designated as an honorary separated member of the Space Force. An eligible individual so designated may be referred to as a Legacy Guardian.
Regulations prescribed under this section may include the following elements:

paragraph.text: Eligibility criteria, including applicable dates of service and constructive service credit, for designation under this section.
An application process through which an eligible individual, or a survivor of a deceased eligible individual, may apply for such designation of such eligible individual.
A certificate, approved device, or other insignia of such designation.

subsection.text: Designation of an eligible individual under this section shall not be construed to entitle such eligible individual to any benefit in addition to those established by this section or pursuant to regulations prescribed under this section.
In this section, the term eligible individual means an individual—

paragraph.text: whom the Secretary of the Air Force determines served in support of space operations as a member of the Air Force; and
who separates (or previously separated) from the armed forces as a member of the Air Force.

section.header: Military personnel: recruiting; merit-based determinations

subsection.text: Not later than September 30, 2024, the Secretary of Defense shall prescribe regulations that any effort to recruit an individual to serve in a covered Armed Force may not take into account the race or gender of such individual.
Not later than September 30, 2024, the Secretary of Defense shall prescribe regulations that, with regards to a military accession, assignment, selection, or promotion—

paragraph.text: a determination shall be made on the basis of merit in order to advance those individuals who exhibit the talent and abilities necessary to promote the national security of the United States;
a candidate shall be evaluated on the bases of qualifications, performance, integrity, fitness, training, and conduct;
no determination may be based on favoritism or nepotism; and
no quota may be used.

subsection.text: In this section, the term covered Armed Force means the following:

paragraph.text: The Army.
The Navy.
The Marine Corps.
The Air Force.
The Space Force.

section.header: Improvements to medical standards for accession to certain Armed Forces

subsection.text: Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, and every two years thereafter, the Secretary of Defense shall—

paragraph.text: conduct an assessment of the prescribed medical standards and medical screening processes required for the appointment of an individual as an officer, or enlistment of an individual as a member, in each covered Armed Force;
taking into account the findings of such assessment—

subparagraph.text: update such standards and processes, as may be necessary; and
take such steps as may be necessary to improve the waiver process for individuals who do not meet such prescribed medical standards; and

paragraph.text: submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the House of Representatives and the Senate a report containing, with respect to the most recently conducted assessment under paragraph (1)—

subparagraph.text: the findings of that assessment and a description of the actions carried out pursuant to paragraph (2); and
recommendations by the Secretary for any legislative action the Secretary determines necessary to further improve such standards and processes.

subsection.text: In this section, the term covered Armed Force means the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, or Space Force.

section.header: Protections for members of certain Armed Forces who refuse to receive vaccinations against COVID-19

subsection.text: The Secretary of the military department concerned may not take any adverse action against a member of a covered Armed Force solely on the basis that such member refuses to receive a vaccination against COVID-19.

paragraph.text: At the request of a covered individual during the two years following the date of the involuntary separation of the covered individual, the Secretary of the military department concerned shall consider reinstating such covered individual—

subparagraph.text: as a member of the covered Armed Force concerned; and
in the grade held by such covered individual immediately before the involuntary separation of the covered individual.

paragraph.header: Treatment of period between separation and reinstatement
paragraph.text: The Secretary of the military department concerned shall treat the period of time between the involuntary separation of a covered individual and the reinstatement of such covered individual under paragraph (1) as a period of inactivation from active service under the following provisions of section 710 of title 10, United States Code:

subparagraph.text: Subsection (b).
Subparagraphs (B) through (D) of paragraph (2) of subsection (f).
Paragraph (4) of subsection (f).
Subsection (g).

subsection.text: In this section:

paragraph.text: The term covered Armed Force means the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, or Space Force.
The term covered individual means an individual involuntarily separated from a covered Armed Force solely on the basis of the refusal of such individual to receive a vaccination against COVID-19.

section.header: Reviews of characterization of administrative discharges of certain members on the basis of failure to receive COVID-19 vaccine

subsection.text: A board established under section 1553 of title 10, United States Code, shall grant a request pursuant to such section to review the characterization of a discharge or dismissal of a former member of a covered Armed Force if such discharge or dismissal was solely based on the failure of such former member to obey a lawful order to receive a vaccine for COVID-19.
A board described in subsection (a) shall consider a request described in such subsection before any other request on the docket of such board.
In this section, the term covered Armed Force means the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, or Space Force.

section.header: Certain members discharged or dismissed on the sole basis of failure to obey a lawful order to receive a vaccine for COVID-19: communication strategy regarding reinstatement process

subsection.text: Not later than six months after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the Secretaries of the military departments, shall communicate, to a covered individual, the current, established, process by which a covered individual may be reinstated in the covered Armed Force concerned.

Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the House of Representatives and the Senate a report on implementation of the communication strategy under subsection (a).
In this section:

paragraph.text: The term covered individual means an individual discharged or dismissed from a covered Armed Force on the sole basis of failure to obey a lawful order to receive a vaccine for COVID-19.
The term covered Armed Force means the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, or Space Force.

section.header: Pilot program on cardiac screenings for military accessions

subsection.text: Not later than September 30, 2024, the Secretary of Defense shall carry out a pilot program to provide an electrocardiogram to individuals who undergo military accession screenings. Each such electrocardiogram shall be provided—

paragraph.text: on a mandatory basis;
at no cost to the recipient; and
in a facility of the Department of Defense or by a member or employee of the military health system.

subsection.text: In carrying out the pilot program, the Secretary shall—

paragraph.text: determine the costs (including protocols and personnel and equipment for each military entrance processing station) and benefits to the Department of providing an electrocardiogram to every individual who undergoes a military accession screening;
develop and implement appropriate processes to assess the long-term impacts of electrocardiogram results on military service; and
consult with experts in cardiology to develop appropriate clinical practice guidelines for cardiac screenings, diagnosis, and treatment.

subsection.text: Not later than 180 days after the date on which the pilot program terminates, the Secretary shall provide to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives a briefing on the pilot program. Such briefing shall include the following:

paragraph.text: The results of all electrocardiograms provided to individuals under the pilot program—

subparagraph.text: disaggregated by Armed Force, race, and gender; and
without any personally identifiable information.

paragraph.text: The rate of significant cardiac issues detected pursuant to electrocardiograms provided under the pilot program, disaggregated by Armed Force, race, and gender.
The number of individuals, if any, who were disqualified from accession based solely on the result of an electrocardiogram provided under the pilot program.
The cost of carrying out the pilot program.

subsection.text: The pilot program shall terminate after three years after its implementation.

section.header: Prohibition on certain communications regarding courts-martial
section.text: Section 837 of title 10, United States Code (article 37 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice), is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection:

paragraph.text: No court-martial convening authority, nor any other commanding officer, may provide a briefing concerning a pending court-martial, or allegations that may lead to a court-martial, to any subordinate who may be selected to serve as a member of such court-martial.
The prohibition in paragraph (1) shall not apply to a briefing provided in the course of a court-martial proceeding to a member of the armed forces who is participating in such proceeding.

section.header: Technical and conforming amendments to the Uniform Code of Military Justice

subsection.header: Technical amendment relating to guilty pleas for murder
subsection.text: Section 918 of title 10, United States Code (article 118 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice), is amended—

paragraph.text: by striking he each place it appears and inserting such person; and

in the matter following paragraph (4), by striking the period and inserting , unless such person is otherwise sentenced in accordance with a plea agreement entered into between the parties under section 853a of this title (article 53a)..

subsection.header: Technical amendments relating to the military justice reforms in the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022

paragraph.text: Subsection (c)(2)(A) of section 816 of title 10, United States Code (article 16 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice), is amended by striking by the convening authority.
Section 825 of title 10, United States Code (article 25 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice), is amended—

subparagraph.text: in subsection (d)—

clause.text: in paragraph (1), by striking may, after the findings are announced and before any matter is presented in the sentencing phase, request, orally on the record or in writing, sentencing by members and inserting shall be sentenced by the military judge; and
by amending paragraph (2) to read as follows:

paragraph.text: In a capital case, if the accused is convicted of an offense for which the court-martial may sentence the accused to death, the accused shall be sentenced in accordance with section 853(c) of this title (article 53(c)).

subparagraph.text: in subsection (e)—

clause.text: in paragraph (1), by striking him and inserting the member being tried; and
in paragraph (2)—

subclause.text: in the first sentence, by striking his opinion and inserting the opinion of the convening authority; and
in the second sentence, by striking he and inserting the member; and

subparagraph.text: in subsection (f) in the second sentence—

clause.text: by striking his authority and inserting the authority of the convening authority; and
by striking his staff judge advocate or legal officer and inserting the staff judge advocate or legal officer of the convening authority.

subsection.header: Authority of special trial counsel with respect to certain offenses occurring before effective date of military justice reforms enacted in the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022

paragraph.text: Section 824a of title 10, United States Code, as added by section 531 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (Public Law 117–81; 135 Stat. 1692), is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection:

subsection.header: Special trial counsel authority over certain other offenses

paragraph.text: A special trial counsel may, at the sole and exclusive discretion of the special trial counsel, exercise authority over the following offenses:

subparagraph.text: An offense under section 917a (article 117a), 918 (article 118), section 919 (article 119), section 920 (article 120), section 920b (article 120b), section 920c (article 120c), section 928b (article 128b), or the standalone offense of child pornography punishable under section 934 (article 134) of this title that occurred on or before December 27, 2023.
An offense under section 925 (article 125), section 930 (article 130), or section 932 (article 132) of this title that occurred on or after January 1, 2019, and before December 28, 2023.
An offense under section 925 (article 125) of this title alleging an act of nonconsensual sodomy that occurred before January 1, 2019.
A conspiracy to commit an offense specified in subparagraph (A), (B), or (C) as punishable under section 881 of this title (article 81).
A solicitation to commit an offense specified in subparagraph (A), (B), or (C) as punishable under section 882 of this title (article 82).
An attempt to commit an offense specified in subparagraph (A), (B), (C), (D), or (E) as punishable under section 880 of this title (article 80).

If a special trial counsel exercises authority over an offense pursuant to paragraph (1), the offense over which the special trial counsel exercises authority shall be considered a covered offense for purposes of this chapter.

If a special trial counsel exercises authority over an offense pursuant to paragraph (1), the special trial counsel may exercise the authority of the special trial counsel under subsection (c)(2)(B) with respect to other offenses described in that subparagraph without regard to the date on which the other offenses occur.

paragraph.text: Section 539C(a) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (Public Law 117–81; 10 U.S.C. 801 note) is amended by striking and shall and inserting and, except as provided in section 824a(d) of title 10, United States Code (article 24a(d) of the Uniform Code of Military Justice), shall.

subsection.text: The amendments made by subsection (b) and subsection (c)(1) shall take effect immediately after the coming into effect of the amendments made by part 1 of subtitle D of title V of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (Public Law 117–81) as provided in section 539C of that Act (10 U.S.C. 801 note).

section.header: Treatment of certain records of criminal investigations

subsection.text: The Secretary of Defense shall develop and implement uniform guidance providing for the modification of titling and indexing systems to ensure that a record identifying a member or former member of the Armed Forces as the subject of a criminal investigation is removed from such system if that member or former member is cleared of wrongdoing as described in subsection (d).

Not later than 60 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, each Secretary concerned, pursuant to the guidance issued by the Secretary of Defense under subsection (a) and in consultation with the appropriate Judge Advocate General, shall—

paragraph.text: review the titling and indexing systems of the defense criminal investigative organizations under the jurisdiction of such Secretary to identify each record in such system that pertains to a member or former member of the Armed Forces who has been cleared of wrongdoing as described in subsection (d);
notify the defense criminal investigative organization involved of each record identified under paragraph (1); and
direct the head of the organization to remove the record in accordance with subsection (c).

subsection.text: The head of a defense criminal investigative organization that receives a notice under subsection (b)(2) with respect to a record in a titling or indexing system shall ensure that the record is removed from such system by not later than 30 days after the date on which the notice is received.
A member or former member of the Armed Forces who is the subject of a criminal investigation shall be considered to have been cleared of wrongdoing for purposes of subsection (a) if—

paragraph.text: the member or former member is found not guilty at military or civilian trial for the alleged offense;
an investigation conducted by defense criminal investigative organization or another Federal or civilian law enforcement agency determines that—

subparagraph.text: the member or former member is not responsible for the alleged offense; or
was mistakenly identified as a subject;

paragraph.text: the alleged offence was addressed through non-judicial punishment imposed under section 815 of title 10, United States Code (article 15 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice) and the involuntary separation of the member was not required or recommended as part of such punishment;
the investigation into the alleged offense has been open for 10 years or more and charges have not been filed;
the member or former member is pardoned;
the reasons specified for the charges are unsupported by the evidence of the offense a for which the member or former member was under investigation as determined by—

subparagraph.text: a court-martial or other proceeding brought under chapter 47 of title 10, United States Code (the Uniform Code of Military Justice).
an administrative proceeding within the Department of Defense or the Armed Force concerned.
a civilian court; or

paragraph.text: the Government makes a final determination not to prosecute the member or former member for the criminal offense for which the member or former member was under investigation.

subsection.text: No member of an Armed Force may be involuntarily separated solely for—

paragraph.text: an offense for which the member is cleared of wrongdoing as described in subsection (d); or
an offense for which the punishment of separation was not specifically recommended—

subparagraph.text: by a court-martial under chapter 47 of title 10, United States Code (the Uniform Code of Military Justice); or
by a commander pursuant to the commander’s authority to impose non-judicial punishment under section 815 of such chapter (article 15 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice).

subsection.text: The requirements of this section are in addition to any requirements imposed under section 549 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (Public Law 117–263). This section shall supercede any provision of section 549 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (Public Law 117–263) that is inconsistent with this section, but only to the extent of the inconsistency.
In this section:

paragraph.text: The term defense criminal investigative organization means—

subparagraph.text: the Army Criminal Investigation Command;
the Naval Criminal Investigative Service;
the Air Force Office of Special Investigations;
the Coast Guard Investigative Service;
the Defense Criminal Investigative Service; and
any other organization or element of the Department of Defense or an Armed Force that is responsible for conducting criminal investigations.

paragraph.text: The term promotion board has the meaning given such term in section 628 of title 10, United States Code.
The term Secretary concerned has the meaning given that term in section 101 of title 10, United States Code.
The term selection board has the meaning given such term in section 1558 of title 10, United States Code.

The term titling and indexing system means any database or other records system used by a defense criminal investigative organization for purposes of titling and indexing (as those terms are defined in section 549(g) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (Public Law 117–263)), including the Defense Central Index of Investigations (commonly known as DCII).

section.header: Limitation on availability of funds for relocation of Army CID special agent training course

subsection.text: None of the funds authorized to be appropriated by this Act or otherwise made available for fiscal year 2024 for the Army may be obligated or expended to relocate an Army CID special agent training course until each of the requirements specified in paragraphs (1) and (2) of section 548(a) of the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (Public Law 117–263) have been met.

In this section, the terms relocate and Army CID special agent training course have the meanings given those terms in section 548(b) of the James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2023 (Public Law 117–263).

section.header: Supreme Court review of certain actions of the United States Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces

subsection.header: Certiorari to the United States Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces

paragraph.text: Section 1259 of title 28, United States Code, is amended—

subparagraph.text: in paragraph (3), by inserting or denied after granted; and
in paragraph (4), by inserting or denied after granted.

Section 867a(a) of title 10, United States Code (article 67a of the Uniform Code of Military Justice), is amended by striking The Supreme Court may not review by a writ of certiorari under this section any action of the United States Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces in refusing to grant a petition for review..

subparagraph.header: Time for application for writ of certiorari
subparagraph.text: Section 2101(g) of title 28, United States Code, is amended to read as follows:

subsection.text: The time for application for a writ of certiorari to review a decision of the United States Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces, or the decision of a Court of Criminal Appeals that the United States Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces refuses to grant a petition to review, shall be as prescribed by rules of the Supreme Court.

paragraph.text: Subject to paragraph (2), the amendments made by subsection (a) shall take effect upon the expiration of the 180-day period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act and shall apply to any petition granted or denied by the United States Court of Appeals for the Armed Forces on or after that effective date.

The authority of the Supreme Court to prescribe rules to carry out section 2101(g) of title 28, United States Code, as amended by subsection (a)(2)(B) of this section, shall take effect on the date of the enactment of this Act.

section.header: Study on removal of Sexual Assault Victim Advocates from the chain of command of victims

subsection.text: The Secretary of Defense shall conduct a study to determine—

paragraph.text: the feasibility and advisability of requiring that any Sexual Assault Victim Advocate assigned to a victim under section 1565b of title 10, United States Code, be from outside the chain of command of the victim; and
the potential effects of such a requirement on the ability of the Armed Forces to implement sexual assault prevention and response programs.

subsection.text: Not later than one year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Secretary of Defense shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives a report on the results of the study conducted under subsection (a).

section.header: Military education for special operations forces

subsection.text: Section 167 of title 10, United States Code, is amended as follows:

paragraph.text: In subsection (e)(2), by adding at the end the following new subparagraph:

subparagraph.text: Providing for the education of members of the special operations forces at degree-granting institutions of higher military education.

paragraph.text: In subsection (g)—

subparagraph.text: in paragraph (1), by striking and at the end;
in paragraph (2), by striking the period at the end and inserting ; and; and
by adding at the end the following:

paragraph.text: joint special operations-peculiar education, leader preparation, and leader development, including payment of tuition fees for members attending degree-granting education programs.
By adding at the end the following new subsection:

subsection.text: In this section:

paragraph.text: The term degree-granting institutions of higher military education means—

subparagraph.text: the professional military education schools;
the senior level service schools;
the intermediate level service schools;
the joint intermediate level service school;
the Naval Postgraduate School;
the United States Air Force Institute of Technology; and
the Service Academies.

paragraph.text: The terms intermediate level service school, joint intermediate level service school, and senior level service school have the meaning given such terms in section 2151 of this title.
The term professional military education schools means the schools specified in section 2162 of this title.
The term Service Academy has the meaning given such term in section 347 of this title.

The term special operations-peculiar academic education means education at degree-granting institutions of higher military education that involves or impacts the United States Special Operations Command.

subsection.text: Consistent with such regulations as the Secretary of Defense may prescribe to carry out the amendments made this section, the Commander of the United States Special Operations Command may expend funds appropriated for Major Force Program 11 for fiscal year 2024 or subsequent fiscal years to support special operations-peculiar academic education at degree-granting institutions of higher military education.

section.header: Expansion of individuals eligible to serve as administrators and instructors in the Junior Reserve Officers' Training Corps
section.text: Section 2031 of title 10, United States Code, is amended—

paragraph.text: by striking subsections (e) and (f) and redesignating subsections (g) and (h) as subsections (e) and (f), respectively; and
by amending subsection (d) to read as follows:

Instead of, or in addition to, detailing officers and noncommissioned officers on active duty under subsection (c)(1), the Secretary of the military department concerned may authorize qualified institutions to employ, as administrators and instructors in the program, applicants who are—

subparagraph.text: retired officers and noncommissioned officers whose qualifications are approved by the Secretary and the institution concerned;
officers and noncommissioned officers who—

clause.text: have completed at least eight years of service in the armed forces;
have received honorable discharges not longer than five years before applying for such employment; and
are approved by the Secretary of the military department concerned and the institution concerned;

subparagraph.text: officers and noncommissioned officers who are in an active status; or
officers and noncommissioned officers—

clause.text: who are under 60 years of age;
who but for age, would be eligible for retired pay for non-regular service under section 12731 of this title; and
whose qualifications are approved by the Secretary of the military department concerned and the institution concerned.

paragraph.text: Employment under this subsection shall be subject to the following conditions:

subparagraph.text: The Secretary of Defense shall prescribe a joint service instructor pay scale system to pay administrators and instructors employed under this subsection.

Subject to subparagraph (C), the Secretary of the military department concerned shall pay to an institution that employs an administrator or instructor under this subsection an amount equal to one-half of the pay paid by the Secretary of the military department concerned to such individual for any period.
The Secretary of the military department concerned may pay the institution more than the amount set forth in subparagraph (B) if the Secretary concerned determines that—

clause.text: the institution is in an educationally and economically deprived area; and
such action is in the national interest.

subparagraph.text: Payments by the Secretary of the military department concerned under this subsection shall be made from funds appropriated for such purpose.
The Secretary of the military department concerned may require an individual employed under this subsection to transfer to the Individual Ready Reserve.

section.header: Prohibition of establishment or maintenance of a unit of the Junior Reserve Officers' Training Corps at an educational institution owned, operated, or controlled by the Chinese Communist Party
section.text: Section 2031 of title 10, United States Code, as amended by section 552, is further amended by adding at the end the following new subsection:

subsection.text: No unit may be established or maintained at an educational institution that is owned, operated, or controlled by a person that—

paragraph.text: is the People’s Republic of China;
is a member of the Chinese Communist Party;
is a member of the People’s Liberation Army;

is identified by the Secretary of Defense under section 1260H(a) of the William M. (Mac) Thornberry National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 (10 U.S.C. 113 note) as a Chinese military company;
is included in the Non-SDN Chinese Military-Industrial Complex Companies List published by the Department of the Treasury; or
is owned by or controlled by or is an agency or instrumentality of any person described in paragraphs (1) through (5).

section.header: Inclusion of advanced research programs at certain institutions of professional military education

subsection.header: United States Army Command and General Staff College
subsection.text: Chapter 751 of title 10, United States Code is amended by adding at the end the following new section:

section.header: Establishment of advanced research program at the United States Army Command and General Staff College
section.text: Under regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Army, the President of the United States Army Command and General Staff College shall establish, within the College, an advanced research program that examines the character of near-future operational-tactical warfighting at the high end of the conflict spectrum in East Asia. The program shall use wargaming, operations research, and systems analysis as the primary methodologies for developing scenarios for analysis under the program.

subsection.text: Chapter 859 of title 10, United States Code is amended by adding at the end the following new section:

section.header: Establishment of advanced research program at the Naval War College
section.text: Under regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Navy, the President of the Naval War College shall establish, within the College, an advanced research program that examines the character of near-future operational-tactical warfighting at the high end of the conflict spectrum in East Asia. The program shall use wargaming, operations research, and systems analysis as the primary methodologies for developing scenarios for analysis under the program.

subsection.text: Chapter 951 of title 10, United States Code is amended by inserting after section 9420 the following new section:

section.header: Establishment of advanced research program at the Air University
section.text: Under regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Air Force, the Commander of the Air University shall establish, within the University, an advanced research program that examines the character of near-future operational-tactical warfighting at the high end of the conflict spectrum in East Asia. The program shall use wargaming, operations research, and systems analysis as the primary methodologies for developing scenarios for analysis under the program.

subsection.text: Not later than February 1 of each year, the President of the United States Army Command and General Staff College, the President of the Naval War College, and the Commander of the Air University shall each provide to the Committees on Armed Services of the Senate and the House of Representatives a briefing on wargaming outcomes and force structure recommendations resulting from activities conducted under the advanced research programs established under sections 7423, 8596, and 9421 of title 10, United States Code, respectively.

section.header: Pilot program for enlisted members of the Army and the Navy to attend the Naval Postgraduate School

subsection.text: During fiscal year 2024, the Secretaries of the Army and the Navy shall each implement a pilot program to send enlisted members of the Army and the Navy, respectively, to earn master’s degrees at NPS, in programs determined appropriate by each such Secretary in coordination with the President of NPS.
A member of the Army or Navy shall be eligible to participate in such a pilot program on the same bases as a member of the Marine Corps pursuant to the MCGEP-E Pilot.

The Secretary concerned shall select a member who applies to participate in such a pilot program on the same bases used to select a member of the Marine Corps pursuant to the MCGEP-E Pilot. Each Secretary concerned shall select a number of participants that equals the number of officers of the Armed Force concerned who attend NPS at the same time.
The Secretary concerned shall promote a pilot program under this section to encourage members to apply.

The Secretary concerned shall ensure that the duties of a member selected to participate in such a pilot program are performed by another member of the Armed Force concerned until the participant returns to such duties.
Each such pilot program shall terminate six years after commencement.

Not more than one year after the completion of a pilot program, each Secretary concerned, in coordination with the Secretary of Defense, shall submit to the Committees on Armed Services of the House of Representatives and Senate a report on the pilot program. Each such report shall include the following:

paragraph.text: The evaluation of the Secretary concerned of the effects of the pilot program on—

subparagraph.text: the career trajectories of participants (including effects on pay);
retention of participants;
recruitment;
job performance of participants;
merit-based promotions of participants; and
objectives outlined in the 2022 National Defense Strategy to modernize the Armed Forces, spur innovation, and outpace and outthink adversaries of the United States;

paragraph.text: The recommendation of the Secretary concerned regarding whether to make the pilot program permanent.
An estimate of funding and any legislation necessary to make the pilot program permanent.
Other matters the Secretary concerned determines appropriate.

subsection.text: In this section:

paragraph.text: The term MCGEP-E Pilot means the Fiscal Year 2023 Marine Corps Graduate Education Program – Enlisted Pilot Program.
The term NPS means the Naval Postgraduate School.

section.header: Increase in accession bonus for nurse officer candidates
section.text: Section 2130a(a) of title 10, United States Code, is amended—

by striking $10,000 and inserting $20,000.

subsection.text: Section 7442 of title 10, United States Code, is amended—

in subsection (b)(5), by striking 150 and inserting 250.
